description: Reviewed plain-English word explanations for Genesis chapter 1, keyed by Strong's ID. Meanings depend on verse context; the original Hebrew corpus and legacy dictionary remain intact.

entries.H7225: The beginning—the very start. Genesis opens by showing us God at the beginning of everything.
entries.H1254: To create, to bring into being. Here, God is the One who brings the heavens and earth into being.
entries.H430: God. Here, this Hebrew word names the one God who creates.
entries.H853: A small Hebrew marker that points to what receives the action. English usually leaves it quiet, but Hebrew uses it to make the sentence clear.
entries.H8064: The heavens or sky—everything above the earth. Here, it belongs to the whole world God creates.
entries.H776: The earth or land—the ground beneath our feet and the world where life takes shape. The verse shows which meaning fits.
entries.H1961: To be, become, or happen. In this chapter it can mean “was,” “came to be,” or “let there be,” depending on the line.
entries.H8414: Wild, empty, without shape. The earth is not ready for life yet; God is about to bring order to it.
entries.H922: Empty, with nothing filling it. Alongside the previous word, it paints a world still waiting to be made ready for life.
entries.H2822: Darkness—the absence of light. At the start, darkness covers the deep, but it will not have the final word.
entries.H5921: On, over, above, or upon. This little word shows where one thing rests in relation to another.
entries.H6440: Face, front, or surface. Here it means the surface of the deep waters.
entries.H8415: The deep—the great waters stretching out before the land appears.
entries.H7307: Wind, breath, or spirit. Here, God’s Spirit is moving over the waters while the world is still taking shape.
entries.H7363: To hover or move gently, like a bird over its young. The picture here is of God’s Spirit moving over the waters.
entries.H4325: Water or waters. At this point in the story, the waters cover the earth before dry land appears.
entries.H559: To speak or say. God speaks, and creation answers.
entries.H216: Light—the brightness that lets us see. God calls it forth, and the darkness gives way.
entries.H7200: To see, look at, or notice. God looks at what He has made and sees it clearly.
entries.H3588: Because, that, or when. It joins one thought to another, and the sentence tells us which meaning belongs.
entries.H2896: Good—pleasing, right, just as it should be. God looks at what He has made and calls it good.
entries.H914: To separate, to set things apart. God gives light and darkness their own places.
entries.H996: Between. This word marks the space or boundary that keeps two things apart.
entries.H7121: To call, name, or announce. God gives names to what He has made.
entries.H3117: Day—the daylight hours or the whole day, depending on the line.
entries.H3915: Night—the dark part of the day, when the sun is no longer shining.
entries.H6153: Evening—the hour when daylight fades and night begins.
entries.H1242: Morning—the first light as night gives way to a new day.
entries.H259: One, a single thing, or first in a count. Here, it helps mark the days of creation.
entries.H7549: A wide space above the earth. In this scene, it is the sky God places between the waters.
entries.H8432: The middle or inside of something. Here, God places the expanse in the middle of the waters.
entries.H6213: To do or make—to bring something about. God makes the parts of creation He has spoken into being.
entries.H834: Which, that, who, or what. This small word connects a description to the person or thing being described.
entries.H8478: Underneath or below. It shows where the lower waters are in relation to the sky.
entries.H3651: And so it was. God spoke, and what He said came to pass.
entries.H8145: Second—the next one in the order. Here, evening and morning bring the second day to its close.
entries.H6960: To gather things together. God calls the waters to come together in one place, and dry land appears.
entries.H413: To or toward. A small word that shows where something is headed.
entries.H4725: A place—a spot where something belongs. Here, the waters are gathered into their place.
entries.H3004: Dry ground, the firm land that rises above the water.
entries.H3220: The sea—a large body of water gathered apart from the dry land.
entries.H1876: To sprout, to bring up new growth. God calls the earth to bring forth plants.
entries.H1877: Grass and fresh green growth coming up from the ground.
entries.H6212: Plants and herbs—the green life the earth brings up.
entries.H2232: To sow or scatter seed so something can grow.
entries.H2233: Seed—the small beginning of another plant, carrying life forward.
entries.H6086: A tree, or the wood it gives. Here, the word points to trees growing on the land.
entries.H6529: Fruit—the growth a tree or plant bears, often carrying seed for what comes next.
entries.H3318: To come out or bring forth. Here, the earth brings plants and trees out into the open.
entries.H7992: Third—the next day in the order. This marks the day the land and plants appear.
entries.H3974: A light or something that gives light. Here, God sets lights in the sky.
entries.H226: A sign or marker that points something out. The lights mark days, seasons, and years.
entries.H4150: A set time or season—an occasion that comes around in its appointed time.
entries.H8141: A year—a full cycle of time.
entries.H215: To shine, to give light. The lights in the sky shine down on the earth.
entries.H8147: Two, a pair. Here, it points to the two great lights God sets in the sky.
entries.H1419: Great, large, or important. Here, it describes the greater light that rules the day.
entries.H6996: Small or little. Here, it describes the light that rules the night.
entries.H3556: A star—a light in the night sky. Even the stars belong to what God has made.
entries.H5414: To give, put, or place. God sets the lights in the sky where they belong.
entries.H4910: To rule or govern—to have charge over something. The lights mark the rhythm of day and night.
entries.H7243: Fourth—the fourth day in the story, when God sets lights in the sky.
entries.H8317: To swarm, to move in great numbers. The waters teem with living creatures.
entries.H8318: A swarm—a whole mass of creatures moving through the water.
entries.H5315: A living being, a creature, or a life. Here, God fills the waters and sky with living creatures.
entries.H2416: Alive—full of life. The waters and sky are no longer empty; life is moving everywhere.
entries.H5775: Birds and other flying creatures—the life filling the sky.
entries.H5774: To fly through the air. The birds spread their wings across the open sky.
entries.H8577: A great creature of the sea. Here, even the mighty creatures in the waters are made by God.
entries.H3605: All, every, the whole. Nothing is left outside the word’s reach.
entries.H7430: To move about, crawl, or creep along the ground.
entries.H3671: A wing—the part that lifts a bird into the air.
entries.H1288: To bless—to give good things and make room for life to thrive. God blesses the creatures and tells them to fill the waters and sky.
entries.H6509: To bear fruit or have young—to bring forth more life.
entries.H7235: To grow many, to increase, to multiply. Life is given room to spread.
entries.H4390: To fill something up. God tells living creatures to fill the waters and the earth.
entries.H2549: Fifth—the fifth day, when the waters and sky fill with life.
entries.H929: Land animals, especially the larger animals that live on the ground.
entries.H7431: A creature that moves along the ground—small or large, creeping or crawling.
entries.H127: Ground or soil—the earth beneath our feet.
entries.H120: A human being, a person, or humankind. Here, God creates people.
entries.H6754: An image or likeness—a reflection of someone. People are made in God’s image to represent Him in the world He made.
entries.H1823: A likeness or resemblance—being like someone. People are made to reflect God.
entries.H7287: To rule or have authority. People are given responsibility for the creatures God made.
entries.H1710: Fish—the creatures that move through the waters.
entries.H2145: Male—a word describing a male person or animal.
entries.H5347: Female—a word describing a female person or animal.
entries.H3533: To bring under control or subdue. People are told to take responsibility for the earth and its life.
entries.H2009: Look—pay attention. The word calls us to notice what God has placed right before us.
entries.H402: Food—the things living creatures eat to live.
entries.H3418: Green or fresh-growing. Here, it describes the plants God gives for food.
entries.H3966: Very—more than good. God looks at everything He has made, and it is very good.
entries.H8345: Sixth—the sixth day, when God creates people and land animals.
entries.H4723: A gathered place or collection of water. Here, the seas are the waters gathered together.
entries.H4327: A kind, type, or family. The verse shows life bearing more life according to its kind.
entries.H4475: Rule or authority—the work the lights are given as they mark day and night.
